question: Should OpenClaw core adopt ordered, immutable startup configuration layers as a supported Gateway CLI and lifecycle contract?
rationale: The patch adds a substantial new public configuration mode whose write, reload, ownership, and operator semantics are not established by current behavior, while the linked RFC remains open.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded core mode
options.body: Approve the startup-only layered contract, then require path-scoped write ownership and upgrade-focused validation before merge.

options.title: Keep composition external
options.body: Continue requiring hosts to materialize one canonical validated config before launching OpenClaw.

options.title: Expose a narrower owner seam
options.body: Add only the generic config-owner API needed for an external launcher or plugin to implement managed composition.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded core mode
recommendation.body: Approve the startup-only layered contract, then require path-scoped write ownership and upgrade-focused validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person most directly to Gateway startup, migrations, and configuration validation—the central lifecycle surfaces affected by this decision.
